name: Alvimopan after radical cystectomy
question: Does perioperative alvimopan accelerate gastrointestinal recovery compared with placebo after radical cystectomy?

design.population: Patients undergoing radical cystectomy who were scheduled to receive postoperative intravenous opioid patient-controlled analgesia.
design.locator: Full text, Methods, pp 266-267; Fig. 1; Table 1

verdictNote: GI-2 recovery was faster in the 277-patient modified intention-to-treat analysis.
takeaway: In the modified intention-to-treat analysis after radical cystectomy, oral alvimopan versus placebo shortened Kaplan–Meier mean GI-2 recovery (5.5 versus 6.8 days; HR 1.773, 95% CI 1.4-2.3; p < 0.0001) and mean hospital stay (7.44 versus 10.07 days).

results.measure: Time to both first solid-food tolerance and first bowel movement, days
results.note: Kaplan-Meier mean, with 10-day observation censoring; 12% versus 25% did not achieve GI-2 before discharge or day 10. Three placebo patients were excluded from MITT.

results.measure: Kaplan-Meier mean time from end of surgery to discharge order, days; censored at 10 days
results.note: Second endpoint in the prespecified sequential testing order; 11% versus 27% were censored before discharge or day 10.
results.locator: Full text, Methods, pp 266-267; Results, p 267; Table 2 and note, p 269

results.measure: Mean postoperative hospital length of stay, days; mean difference in days
results.note: Third endpoint in the prespecified sequential testing order; difference in days, alvimopan minus placebo, as reported in Table 2.
results.locator: Full text, Methods, pp 266-267; Table 2, p 269

results.measure: Patients with postoperative ileus-related morbidity; risk difference in percentage points
results.note: Fourth endpoint in the prespecified sequential testing order; includes nasogastric tube insertion (7.7% versus 24.6%), prolonged stay due to ileus, or ileus readmission within 7 days (one patient per arm).
results.locator: Full text, Methods, p 266; Results, pp 267-268; Table 2, p 269; Fig. 3, p 270

delivery.label: Assigned oral dose
delivery.note: One dose 30 minutes to 5 hours before surgery, then twice daily until discharge or 7 days; maximum 15 inpatient doses. Both arms had ambulation encouraged on postoperative day 1, liquids offered on day 3, solids on day 4, no epidural analgesia, and at most two opioid-sparing NSAID doses.

delivery.label: Surgical approach and operative duration
delivery.note: Among 21 high-volume academic sites; urinary diversion types differed between arms.
